newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany sees chance to halt rise in jobless.
newsitem.headline: Germany sees chance to halt rise in jobless.

text.p: The strengthening of the German economy next year could stop unemployment from rising but is not expected to put large numbers of people in work, a senior German labour office official said on Thursday.

"If we see a strengthening of the economy in 1997 -- and nobody sees a danger of a slump in 1997 -- we could see the rise in unemployment come to a halt or possibly a moderate rise of the numbers in work," Hanspeter Leikeb, head of the labour office's research arm, told Reuters.
He added, however, that rising numbers in work would be the effect of a broadening of the labour market and would only minimally affect the average jobless figures.
The construction would remain very difficult in 1997 and there is still no evidence of the turnaround.
Job growth will come from the manufacturing sector and supplier and services industries. A decisive factor in overall economic growth will be domestic investment.
"We are seeing growth in exports and consumption," he said.
